subject: How to use the ncores parameter in secr.fit() function .

messages.author: f418045e0cf45abe
messages.subject: How to use the ncores parameter in secr.fit() function .
parts:
Hi, 
I am doing some likelihood analysis in R using the secr package. The boundary I am struct into is that when implementing the logic it is only using one core(R is single-threaded), but there is one parameter in your secr.fit() "ncores=1", when I am not getting it. Is it being used to run the function/analysis on multiple cores or it mean something else. 

Regards 
Sachin Vardhan

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: How to use the ncores parameter in secr.fit() function .
parts:
The help for secr.fit says

"If ncores > 1 the parallel package will be used to create processes on multiple cores (see Parallel for more). Specifying extra cores may improve the speed of multi-session analyses (it may also slow them down, as data must be copied back and forth). There is presently no benefit for single-session analyses."

See ?Parallel for more

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: How to use the ncores parameter in secr.fit() function .
parts: Basically, don't do it. In the current version of secr you won't gain anything unless perhaps you are already fitting a multi-session model. This may change in future. If speed is really an issue then find other ways to speed up the analysis - combining occasions, reducing the number of mask points etc.
